prospective_scoring_rule: A forecast is eligible for scoring only if scored=true and its created_date is on or before its forecast publication date. Retrospective decompositions are preserved for methodological transparency but excluded from Brier scores and calibration.

protocol.calibration_policy: Report Brier scores for all resolved core forecasts and separately by event family and comparable horizon only when sample size is adequate; never imply meaningful calibration from very small cells.
protocol.change_policy: Protocol v1 is frozen for prospective use. Substantive changes require a new numbered protocol version, an effective date, a change log, and no retroactive application to already-issued forecasts.

core_scored_set.resolution: Sustained major interstate strikes lasting at least 72 hours, or a material expansion of major combat to an additional sovereign state or operational theater. Isolated interceptions, one-off strikes, proxy attacks, and rhetoric alone are excluded unless they initiate the qualifying sustained episode.

Replacement of the Islamic Republic's governing constitutional-institutional order, or loss of its effective national governing authority. Leadership succession, cabinet changes, and factional turnover within the same governing order are excluded.

Depreciation of the parallel-market rial by at least 25% against the U.S. dollar over any rolling 30-calendar-day window, using the designated consistent parallel-rate series and excluding a single-day quote anomaly that reverses within 48 hours.
core_scored_set.threshold_note: The 25%/30-day threshold is a monitoring convention chosen ex ante for Protocol v1 for scoreability and sensitivity to acute depreciation; it is not claimed to be a universal economic definition. Sensitivity at 20% and 30% will be reported when resolving.

core_scored_set.resolution: Corroborated settlement disruption lasting at least 14 days in at least two essential-import categories—food or grain, medicine or medical inputs, or critical energy or industrial inputs—combined with broad emergency foreign-exchange, import, or payment restrictions or a material shift by suppliers to prepayment or cash because established settlement channels are failing. Evidence must come from at least two independent source streams.

protocol.deadline_convention: Protocol v1 horizons use local-calendar time: 90-day forecasts resolve 90 local calendar days after forecast_open at the same local clock time; 12-month forecasts resolve on the same local calendar date and clock time one year later (Feb 29 maps to Feb 28). Offset may change with daylight-saving time. This convention is executable in the validator.
protocol.display_clarification: Warning colors describe the current state of a diagnostic failure pathway. Forecast probabilities describe the chance of a defined future event by a stated deadline. A severe current warning and a lower future-event probability, or vice versa, are not inherently inconsistent.
protocol.evidence_balance_policy: For each core forecast, preserve material evidence that raises, lowers, or is genuinely ambiguous/neutral. A zero probability revision may be labeled 'offsetting evidence' when meaningful opposing evidence changed but net probability did not.

evidence_impact_scale.major: High-quality evidence of a structural break, threshold crossing, major military/political/economic event, or failure/restoration of a critical mechanism.
evidence_impact_scale.minor: Credible evidence that modestly updates one input but does not alter the central mechanism or threshold state.
evidence_impact_scale.moderate: Corroborated evidence that materially changes a key driver, threshold state, or one core forecast's assessment.

evidence_reliability.High: Primary/direct evidence or multiple independent highly credible sources; direct and current; no material contradiction.
evidence_reliability.Low: Single-source, materially indirect, stale, contested, or weakly observable evidence. Low evidence cannot by itself trigger Critical.
evidence_reliability.Medium: Credible but indirect, incompletely corroborated, or subject to meaningful measurement/reporting uncertainty.
evidence_reliability.Medium-high: Credible and substantially direct evidence with at least one corroborating stream, or exceptionally strong single-source evidence.

protocol.future_research_note: The v1.1 candidate register is non-operative research backlog only. None of its items changes Protocol v1.0, forecast definitions, warning thresholds, scoring, or the 2026-10-04 workflow unless adopted prospectively in a later numbered protocol.

Physical delivery/blockade.high: Severe route denial/blockade or repeated delivery failure
Physical delivery/blockade.low: Routine evasion/managed delivery with limited disruption
Physical delivery/blockade.mid: Persistent disruption/workarounds and meaningful delivery uncertainty

Sovereign/counterparty.high: Repeated nonperformance or acute sovereign stress

haircut_protocol.dependence_rule: Component contributions are not simply interpreted as independent risks. Protocol v1 applies a 20% overlap deduction to the combined delivery + sanctions/payment + political-tail subtotal above 20 percentage points, rounded to the nearest point, to reduce double counting of a common geopolitical shock.
haircut_protocol.overlap_status: The 20% overlap factor is an explicit Protocol v1 convention, not an empirically estimated correlation parameter. It is a candidate for empirical revision only in a future protocol version.
haircut_protocol.sensitivity: Alongside the v1 20% overlap convention, report sensitivity using 0%, 20%, and 40% overlap deductions. The 20% case remains the Protocol v1 headline; sensitivity cases are diagnostic and do not change the frozen rule.

houthi_protocol.elicitation: Assess matériel and technical/financial support separately from local capability; headline probability is a judgment conditioned on at least one Iranian-support channel remaining strategically meaningful.
houthi_protocol.headline_resolution: Yes only if Iranian matériel or Iranian technical/financial support remains sufficient to measurably sustain advanced Houthi missile/UAV or maritime capability. Houthi independent/local capability alone cannot resolve Iranian-support continuity Yes.

id_policy.evidence_id: Persistent event/source identifier. Reuse the same evidence_id when evidence is carried forward; mark evidence_status='new' or 'carried_forward' rather than creating a duplicate observation.
id_policy.forecast_id: core event id + '_' + forecast date YYYYMMDD; immutable once issued.

protocol.noncore_policy: Other probabilities may be published as diagnostic estimates but are not part of the permanent core scored set unless added prospectively in a later protocol version.
protocol.publication_architecture: Current Pages source is main. Protocol v1 publication procedure validates the proposed record before commit and CI validates again after push. A future candidate-branch/merge gate is preferred for stronger pre-main atomicity; until implemented, a failed CI run must not be represented as validated.

resolution_policy.authority: Resolve from the pre-specified event rule using the archived public evidence record. Ambiguous cases require a written resolution note citing the decisive evidence and rule clause.
resolution_policy.indeterminate: If reliable public evidence is insufficient to determine Yes or No by the resolution review date, code outcome='indeterminate'. Indeterminate forecasts are excluded from Brier/calibration scoring; the exclusion and reason remain public. Never choose a resolution based on which result improves the score.
resolution_policy.review_timing: Perform resolution review promptly after the forecast deadline; later evidence may establish what happened before the deadline only if it directly documents the pre-deadline state.

protocol.revision_attribution_rule: At forecast time, record approximate signed percentage-point contributions for material new evidence/reassessment sufficient to reconcile the prior point forecast to the new point forecast. These are an audit decomposition of judgment, not causal estimates or a statistical model. If effects offset, label offsetting evidence.
protocol.serial_dependence_caveat: Weekly forecasts with overlapping horizons are strongly serially dependent. Per-forecast Brier scores may be reported, but counts of overlapping forecasts must not be interpreted as independent sample size; calibration uncertainty and comparative claims must account for clustering/overlap.
protocol.timestamp_policy: Evidence collection closes before forecast elicitation. Each update records evidence_cutoff as the actual last evidence timestamp used and publication_time as the actual commit/publication timestamp. Material information first available after evidence_cutoff is excluded from that forecast and may enter only the next forecast or an explicitly labeled interim update.
protocol.uncertainty_display: Display the reasonable-analyst interval less prominently than the point forecast and evidence confidence until external forecaster dispersion can be compared with it.

uncertainty_rule.definition: The displayed judgmental uncertainty range is the interval within which the assessor judges that roughly 80% of independent, well-informed analysts using the same public information, event definition and horizon would place their point probability. It measures model/analyst disagreement, not sampling error, a Bayesian credible interval, or the probability that the true probability lies in the interval.
uncertainty_rule.elicitation: Set the point forecast first. Then estimate the 10th and 90th percentiles of the distribution of reasonable analysts' point forecasts without changing the point forecast to center the range.
uncertainty_rule.name: Reasonable-analyst interval

protocol.validation_policy: Errors block validation: malformed core records, wrong deadlines/timestamp ordering, post-cutoff evidence with known publication time, arithmetic failures, or unauthorized historical mutation. Missing precise source publication time is a validation warning and must remain explicitly recorded as unknown.

Evaluate resolution-authority procedures for fragmented or contested national control using experience from resolved forecasts.
Revision attribution: require an explicit residual 'other/model judgment' term and coarse contribution increments so exact reconciliation is not misread as causal precision.
Performance aggregation: account for correlation among core outcomes; report event-family results separately and avoid naive equal-weight aggregate scores that overweight a common crisis process.
Benchmarking: when sample size permits, compare Brier performance with simple benchmarks such as prior-week probability, defensible base rates, and no-change forecasts before claiming skill.

Overlapping-horizon resolution: one qualifying event should resolve every still-open forecast whose event definition and window include it, using the same decisive evidence rather than treating weekly forecasts as independent events.
Resolution records: store outcome, resolution_date, resolved_at, decisive_evidence_ids, and resolution_note for every resolved forecast.
Evidence architecture: consider moving persistent evidence into a global immutable evidence.json with weekly records referencing evidence IDs if carried-forward evidence makes history.json unwieldy.

China oil-credit terminology: evaluate 'equivalent haircut' terminology because risk may be priced through tenor, collateral, quantity, counterparty selection, or payment timing rather than only an explicit price discount.
China haircut uncertainty: separate component/parameter uncertainty from dependence-overlap sensitivity; do not imply overlap is the dominant source of uncertainty.

Houthi quantification: develop diagnostic stock-flow accounting using expenditure/launch rates, replenishment evidence, indigenous-production share, component bottlenecks, and interdiction rates before considering Houthi probabilities for scored status.
Warning-system validation: measure state duration, transition frequency, lead/lag relationship to core forecasts, and whether persistent warning states retain predictive discrimination.
Missingness: distinguish ordinary data gaps from endogenous information suppression such as communications shutdowns or deliberate reporting restrictions.
Source independence: distinguish publisher count from independent underlying information streams and track common-source dependence.

Track prospective-validation maturity explicitly so polished presentation is not mistaken for demonstrated forecast skill; disclose that Protocol v1 initially has little or no resolved prospective record.
Protocol discipline: evaluate the ability to run v1 unchanged for a sustained period, preserve disconfirming evidence, and resolve poor-performing forecasts without retrospective rule changes.

method.label: Model estimate
method.rule: Central haircut = sum of six bounded component haircuts: physical delivery/blockade 0–25 pp; sanctions/payment channels 0–15; sovereign/counterparty 0–10; oil-price/basis 0–8; illiquidity/enforcement 0–8; political/secondary-sanctions tail 0–8. Each component is assigned from documented weekly evidence using Low/Mid/High anchors at 25/50/75% of its cap; the central estimate is the sum rounded to the nearest percentage point. The judgmental range is formed by moving each uncertain component one anchor step down/up, bounded at zero/cap. This is not an observed contract price.

haircut.note: Risk adjustment may appear through price, tenor, collateral or payment timing rather than an explicit discount.

houthi.definition: Strategically meaningful Houthi support is decomposed into Iranian matériel flow, Iranian technical/financial assistance, and Houthi independent/local capability. The headline support-continuity probability refers only to continued Iranian technical/financial or material support sufficient to measurably sustain advanced missile/UAV or maritime capability; local capability alone does not resolve it Yes.

component_rationales.reason: Blockade mostly halted crude exports, but limited product shipments mean physical delivery is impaired, not impossible.
Sanctions and disrupted tanker paths increase payment and correspondent-bank settlement risk.
Severe fiscal constraints increase delayed government/counterparty settlement risk; no sovereign default term is observed.
Changes in market access and routing increase delivered product valuation uncertainty without a verified contract basis.
Limited and irregular transactions face enforcement, liquidity and vessel verification cost.
Escalation and sanctions policy create correlated tail risk; political shocks overlap delivery and payment factors.

forecasts.event_definition: Sustained major interstate strikes lasting at least 72 hours, or a material expansion of major combat to an additional sovereign state or operational theater. Isolated interceptions, one-off strikes, proxy attacks, and rhetoric alone are excluded unless they initiate the qualifying sustained episode.
forecasts.label: Sustained major regional escalation
forecasts.lower: Verified implementation of a negotiated ceasefire or materially restored Hormuz transit under accepted terms.
forecasts.provenance: Prospective four-forecast lock after source-only review; NOT PUBLISHED unless 15-section dual editorial review, full offline validators, PR CI, protected owner merge and canonical verification all pass.
forecasts.raise: A new independently verified sustained interstate-strikes episode, material new-state combat, or accelerated maritime military engagement.

forecasts.event_definition: Replacement of the Islamic Republic's governing constitutional-institutional order, or loss of its effective national governing authority. Leadership succession, cabinet changes, and factional turnover within the same governing order are excluded.
forecasts.label: Regime-ending transition
forecasts.lower: Demonstrated elite cohesion, functioning priority payments and broad stabilization.
forecasts.provenance: Prospective four-forecast lock after source-only review; NOT PUBLISHED unless 15-section dual editorial review, full offline validators, PR CI, protected owner merge and canonical verification all pass.
forecasts.raise: Security force defections, national fiscal payment failure or rival sovereign authority.

forecasts.event_definition: Depreciation of the parallel-market rial by at least 25% against the U.S. dollar over any rolling 30-calendar-day window, using the designated consistent parallel-rate series and excluding a single-day quote anomaly that reverses within 48 hours.
forecasts.label: Currency crisis
forecasts.lower: Sustained parallel-market stability and restored external settlements.
forecasts.provenance: Prospective four-forecast lock after source-only review; NOT PUBLISHED unless 15-section dual editorial review, full offline validators, PR CI, protected owner merge and canonical verification all pass.
forecasts.raise: A consistently measured rapid parallel-rial depreciation and exhaustion of credible support mechanisms.

forecasts.event_definition: Corroborated settlement disruption lasting at least 14 days in at least two essential-import categories—food or grain, medicine or medical inputs, or critical energy or industrial inputs—combined with broad emergency foreign-exchange, import, or payment restrictions or a material shift by suppliers to prepayment or cash because established settlement channels are failing. Evidence must come from at least two independent source streams.
forecasts.label: External-payments crisis
forecasts.lower: Sustained verified essential-import payments through multiple functional channels.
forecasts.provenance: Prospective four-forecast lock after source-only review; NOT PUBLISHED unless 15-section dual editorial review, full offline validators, PR CI, protected owner merge and canonical verification all pass.
forecasts.raise: Corroborated two-category essential-import settlement disruption lasting two weeks and emergency restrictions.

component_rationales.reason: Blockade mostly halted crude exports, but limited product shipments mean physical delivery is impaired, not impossible.
Sanctions and disrupted tanker paths increase payment and correspondent-bank settlement risk.
Severe fiscal constraints increase delayed government/counterparty settlement risk; no sovereign default term is observed.
Changes in market access and routing increase delivered product valuation uncertainty without a verified contract basis.
Limited and irregular transactions face enforcement, liquidity and vessel verification cost.
Escalation and sanctions policy create correlated tail risk; political shocks overlap delivery and payment factors.

method.label: Protocol v1 model estimate
method.rule: Component contributions are not simply interpreted as independent risks. Protocol v1 applies a 20% overlap deduction to the combined delivery + sanctions/payment + political-tail subtotal above 20 percentage points, rounded to the nearest point, to reduce double counting of a common geopolitical shock.

haircut.note: Carried-forward unscored 52-point risk-equivalent model haircut (six components, 4-point overlap deduction; zero/20/40% overlap sensitivity 56/52/48). No authenticated October 25 China oil-credit terms or fresh parameter evidence justify recalibration.

hanke_hyperinflation.assessment: Severe inflation remains historically documented; neither fresh 50% monthly threshold evidence nor a new reliable high-frequency 30-day inflation estimate was admitted.
hanke_hyperinflation.status: October 4 Hanke analysis and 3/6/12-month risk diagnostics retained unchanged; no newer method-consistent monthly rate validated at October 25 cutoff.

houthi.definition: Strategically meaningful Iranian support continues when Iranian matériel assistance or technical and financial support is sufficient to sustain advanced Houthi missile, drone, or maritime capabilities to a measurable degree. Independent Houthi production and locally maintained capabilities, without continuing Iranian assistance, do not qualify as continued Iranian support.
houthi.diagnostic_note: UNSCORED judgmental diagnostics carried from October 18, not new October 25 measurements or scored forecasts. The 6-, 12- and 24-month figures refer to strategically meaningful Iranian support; the 12-month component figures refer to forms of assistance and local capability, not mutually exclusive outcomes or a partition, and may include assistance below the strategically meaningful threshold. Claims of Houthi attacks are not independently verified evidence of fresh Iranian resupply, funding or operational direction. No source in this cutoff supports changing the carried-forward estimates.

updates.limitations: Evidence collection closed before the four prospective forecasts were elicited. Blockade and conflict reporting include interested-party statements and material observation gaps. No verified 25%/30-day rial move, 14-day two-category essential-import settlement crisis, security-force fracture, or new Hanke monthly inflation measurement is claimed. Earlier missing source-publication-time metadata remain explicitly unverified and archived records are unchanged.
methodology_notes: Frozen Protocol v1.0 and previously documented methodology unchanged. October 25 source-only research closed at 14:46:33Z. Two sequential affirmative and critical V10 source-review perspectives were performed in one ChatGPT session, not independent model instances.

Two new original HTML witnesses were verified; 16 source URLs and all six classes were audited. The two accepted maritime measurements have different populations and cannot be divided to create a common attack rate.
Exactly four scored forecasts were opened once, after the source-review seal. No new fiscal, currency, payments or regime observation qualified, so all numerical probabilities remain unchanged.

Publisher first-release timestamps have not been independently authenticated, and Houthi support components remain unscored diagnostics. Source-reliability grading is distinct from confidence in geopolitical direction. The two admitted maritime measurements are scoped differently and do not establish event-specific currency, payments, regime-fracture or ceasefire thresholds. Editorial and validation provenance for the final issued record is documented separately in its dated review receipt.

updates.next_threshold: A regional scored event requires qualifying interstate combat for at least 72 hours or material expansion to another sovereign state or theater; cumulative incident counts alone do not resolve it. A currency event requires at least 25% parallel-rial depreciation across a consistent rolling 30-day series. A payments event requires independently corroborated disruption of at least two essential-import categories for at least 14 days and qualifying restrictions. A regime-end event requires replacement of the governing order or loss of effective national governing authority.
updates.political_resolution_note: The 53/14/17/16 political-outcome partition remains descriptive. The separate scored binary asks whether the governing constitutional-institutional order ends within the next twelve months.
updates.regional_resolution_note: The 7/16/77 descriptive legacy buckets remain unchanged; only the 90-day qualifying interstate-escalation binary forecast is scored. Buckets require explicit mutually exclusive resolution definitions before standalone forecast scoring.

contributions.label: Cumulative IMO incident exposure is severe but does not supply a comparable recent event rate

updates.revision_attribution_status: Frozen Protocol-v1: no numerical revisions to the four probability estimates because the two new eligible maritime observations do not independently support event-specific point changes. Prior probabilities remain October 18; signed contributions and residuals are zero.
updates.social_summary: Iran: maritime risk high; four scored forecasts unchanged.
updates.stabilizer: Lloyd’s documented non-Iranian-linked commercial traffic despite attacks; an earlier original government communiqué urged diplomacy, but no accepted Hormuz reopening or ceasefire has been verified by the two admitted new claims. Continuing traffic alone does not establish essential-import payment continuity.
updates.summary: Severe cumulative maritime incidents coexist with continued but reduced non-Iranian-linked Hormuz traffic. The original-source record supports a limited, mixed risk assessment; it does not independently establish new interstate-entry, regime fracture, 30-day rial-depreciation or essential-import settlement thresholds. The four prospective event probabilities remain unchanged pending better event-specific evidence.

Banking / payments.text: Lloyd’s surviving cargo transits cannot establish essential-import settlement functionality or 14-day two-category disruptions; payment evidence remains inadequate.

Coercive apparatus.text: No direct pre-cutoff verified security-force defection or obedience series; retain unknown status.

Elite cohesion.text: No newly admissible evidence of elite breakup or government replacement; prior institutional-continuity observations carry forward, with partial coverage.

Energy / industrial.text: Confirmed maritime incidents and continued but reduced selected vessel traffic signal logistical strain without quantifying electricity, industrial output or priority allocations.

External support.text: The new source set does not substantiate fresh China settlement, credit or Russian support changes; prior vulnerability indicators are retained but not reverified.

Fiscal.text: No new verified budget, oil-revenue or treasury-payment series; maritime constraints do not independently demonstrate a quantified fiscal deterioration.

Food / medicine.text: September humanitarian context was accessible only as a bulletin landing page, not a fresh independently verified shortage or payments series.

Monetary / FX.text: No new eligible consistent parallel-rial rolling 30-day series was obtained before the October 25 cutoff; the currency-crisis event is unresolved.

Social / protest.text: No newly admitted original report establishes coordinated nationwide protests; lack of sources is not evidence of public acquiescence.

updates.what_changed: IMO reported 120 highlighted confirmed maritime incidents cumulatively across the Strait of Hormuz and wider Middle East as of October 22; the count is not an October-only numerator. Lloyd’s counted 104 versus 126 non-Iranian-linked transits across successive specified weeks; trade has not stopped, but its safety is not demonstrated. These are two different populations, not a computed attack rate.
